purpose: The single source of truth for every quantitative model this project uses. Each entry is a FUNCTION with a declared signature: named inputs with units and domains, a named output, the basis it rests on, a worked example using this project's own measured numbers, and an honest confidence tier. Prose elsewhere in the database may describe these models; this file defines them.
why: The same quantity had been appearing as 'latG', 'lateral G' and 'a + b*v^2' across four files, with units declared in one place and implied in the rest, and project-invented heuristics sitting in the same paragraphs as textbook physics. A reader could not tell which numbers were derived, which were measured, and which were guesses. This registry fixes the notation, states every unit, and tiers every model.

notation.convention: Symbols are lowercase for scalars, subscripted by axle (f = front, r = rear) or by speed (@60, @120). Functions are named in snake_case and always take explicit units. Any value read from the in-game Performance panel is called a READOUT; any value computed here is DERIVED.

symbols.name: speed
symbols.units: mph in readouts, ft/s inside formulas (1 mph = 1.4667 ft/s)

symbols.name: lateral grip at speed v
symbols.source: Performance panel readouts at 60 and 120 mph

symbols.name: mechanical grip coefficient
symbols.meaning: the speed-independent half of latG — tires, weight, springs

symbols.name: aero grip coefficient
symbols.meaning: the speed-squared half of latG — downforce

symbols.name: braking distance from 60 and 100 mph to zero

tiers.physics: Standard vehicle dynamics — holds regardless of what FH6 does internally.
tiers.fitted: A physics-shaped model whose parameters are fitted to in-game readouts. Valid where the readouts are valid.
tiers.heuristic: Invented by this project to compress experience into a number. Useful, directional, NOT a law.
tiers.refuted: Kept on the record because it was believed and then disproved — so nobody re-derives it.

functions.name: Fit the grip curve from two panel readouts
functions.expression:
latG(v) = a + b·v²   where v is in ft/s
b = (latG@120 − latG@60) / (v120² − v60²)
a = latG@60 − b·v60²
with v60 = 88.0 ft/s, v120 = 176.0 ft/s

inputs.read_from: Performance panel, Lateral Gs, 60 mph row
Performance panel, Lateral Gs, 120 mph row

output.name: (a, b)
output.meaning: a = mechanical grip in g; b = aero grip per (ft/s)². Together they define the car's whole grip curve.

functions.basis: Downforce rises with the square of speed; mechanical grip does not. Two readouts at two speeds are exactly enough to separate them.
functions.worked_example:
Viper ACR replica: latG@60 = 1.24, latG@120 = 1.43.
b = (1.43 − 1.24) / (176² − 88²) = 0.19 / 23,232 = 8.18e-6
a = 1.24 − 8.18e-6 × 7,744 = 1.177 g
Read: ~1.18 g of the grip is mechanical and available at any speed; the rest arrives with speed.
functions.caveats: Assumes the two panel readouts are steady-state limits (their in-game description says so). A car with zero downforce gives b ≈ 0, which is the correct answer, not an error.

functions.name: Maximum speed a corner of radius r supports
functions.expression:
Cornering requires v² / r ≤ g·latG(v).
Substituting latG(v) = a + b·v² and solving:
v_max = sqrt( g·r·a / (1 − g·r·b) )   [ft/s, convert to mph by ÷1.4667]
If (1 − g·r·b) ≤ 0 the car is aero-limited nowhere — the corner is theoretically unbounded and the practical limit is elsewhere.

inputs.read_from: estimated from the corner, or solved backwards from a speed you know works

output.name: v_max
output.meaning: the entry speed above which the tires cannot hold this radius, for THIS build

functions.basis: Circular motion: centripetal acceleration v²/r must not exceed available lateral grip.
functions.worked_example:
Viper (a = 1.177, b = 8.18e-6) in a 500 ft corner:
denominator = 1 − 32.17 × 500 × 8.18e-6 = 0.868
v_max = sqrt(32.17 × 500 × 1.177 / 0.868) = sqrt(21,810) = 147.7 ft/s = 101 mph.
Read: that corner is a ~100 mph corner in this car — which is why 110 mph entries kept failing.
functions.caveats: Steady-state only — it says nothing about entry transients, and a car can fail below v_max from a bad brake release. Radius estimates are the weakest input; prefer solving backwards from a speed you have actually held.

functions.name: Aero-brake index — how much of the braking is downforce
functions.expression:
Under constant grip, braking distance scales with v²:  d100 / d60 = (100/60)² = 2.778
index = (d100 / d60) / 2.778

bands.read: strong downforce contribution — lock-resistant at speed, lock-PRONE as it slows
speed-independent grip — the pedal that works at 60 will lock the wheels at 150
brakes worse from high speed than physics predicts — check compound, mass or bias

functions.basis: Kinematics (d = v²/2a) plus the fact that downforce adds vertical load only at speed.
functions.worked_example:
Viper ACR replica: d60 = 79.1 ft, d100 = 195.2 ft.
index = (195.2 / 79.1) / 2.778 = 2.468 / 2.778 = 0.89 → strong aero contribution.
functions.caveats: Derived by this project (the algebra is standard, the diagnostic use is ours). Assumes both readouts come from the same tune state — re-read both after any change.

functions.name: Grip-per-thrust — handling car vs glass rocket

bands.read: glass rocket — power with nothing holding it down
balanced build (every car measured in this project lands here)
handling special — grip bought at the expense of thrust

functions.basis: At a fixed PI cap, power and grip are competing purchases; their ratio reveals which one the builder bought.
functions.worked_example: Viper ACR replica: 1.28 / 0.26 = 4.9. 4C fork A: 1.43 / 0.32 = 4.5. Viper R-class tune: 1.76 / 0.43 = 4.1.
functions.caveats: A COURSE-FIT score, not a quality score — a glass rocket can legitimately win on a straight-heavy lap. The band edges are calibrated on a small sample of this project's own builds.

functions.name: Balance gap — how much the car's personality changes with speed
functions.expression: gap = | mb − ab |   (mechanical balance minus aero balance, both front-share fractions)

bands.read: one consistent car at all speeds
noticeable personality shift as speed rises
two different cars — the machine you learn in hairpins is not the one that arrives at the sweeper

functions.basis: Mechanical grip dominates at low speed and aero at high speed; if their front-shares differ, the effective balance migrates with speed.
functions.worked_example: Viper at the start of tuning: mb 0.64, ab 0.33 → gap 0.31 (two cars). After tuning: mb 0.63, ab 0.57 → gap 0.06 (one car). The player-reported 'lively slow, blind fast' symptom tracked this number.
functions.caveats: The direction of the gap matters as well as its size: aero balance BELOW mechanical means the car understeers more as speed rises; above means it loosens. Band edges are this project's calibration.

functions.name: Aero balance from the downforce sliders
functions.worked_example:
Alfa 4C: 128 front / 208 rear → 128/336 = 0.381, and the panel read 0.38. Exact.
Viper ACR: 457 front / 116 rear → 0.80 predicted, but the panel read 0.57. NOT exact.
functions.why_refuted: Works on some cars and fails on others: the Viper carries large BODY aero contributions at both ends that the sliders never show, so slider ratio ≠ panel balance. Never compute aero balance — READ it from the panel, and recover another car's settings by MATCHING the panel signature rather than calculating it.
functions.caveats: This is the single most instructive failure in the project's modelling: an equation that fit four data points exactly and was still wrong as a general law.

functions.name: Grip versus slip angle (illustrative shape)
functions.expression:
grip(s) = D · x^k · e^( k·(1 − x) )   where x = s / s_peak, D = peak grip, k = sharpness
Peaks at exactly s = s_peak with value D for any k; larger k = sharper cliff.

inputs.typical: 7 slick tarmac, 9 rally tarmac, 22 rally on dirt

functions.basis: A shape function chosen to reproduce the known qualitative behaviour of tire curves (rise, peak, fall) with a single sharpness parameter.
functions.worked_example: Used to draw the Training Zone's three surface curves. At k = 2.2 the slick loses ~15% of peak grip only 4° past the peak; at k = 0.9 the dirt curve is still near peak 10° past it — the cliff-versus-plateau contrast.
functions.caveats: ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY. FH6's real tire model is not published and these parameters are not measured from the game — the curve teaches the concept, it does not predict your car. Do not quote numbers off it.

functions.name: Rescale springs and dampers when build mass changes
functions.expression: k_new = k_old × (m_new / m_old)   — apply the same factor to rebound and bump
functions.basis: Suspension frequency depends on k/m; holding the ratio constant preserves the car's character across a mass change.
functions.worked_example: 4C fork A springs 430/480 at 2,053 lb. Fork B weighs 2,292 lb (+11.6%) → 480/535, with rebound 7.5/8.0 → 8.4/9.0 and bump 4.5/5.0 → 5.0/5.6.
used_by: build sheets when a compound or parts change moves mass
functions.caveats: A slider sheet is only valid at the weight it was derived for. This is the correction that fixed fork B's breakaway-on-turn-in.

functions.name: Recover another tune's cold pressures from telemetry

inputs.read_from: telemetry Tires, Misc. page after 2–3 minutes at pace

output.name: p_cold
output.meaning: the value that was typed into the Tires tab

functions.basis: Observed warm-up rise on this project's own cars (rally compound, 24 psi cold reading 27–28.7 hot).
functions.caveats: The 3.5 psi offset is from ONE car on ONE compound. Compound, driving intensity and session length all change it — measure your own offset before trusting it on a different car.

functions.name: Chassis personality from mass and front bias
functions.expression:
light = m < 2750 lb;  front-biased = f% ≥ 50
(light, front-biased) → Agile & stable
(light, rear-biased) → Nervous & darty
(heavy, front-biased) → Self-damping GT
(heavy, rear-biased) → The handful

output.name: personality
output.meaning: expected yaw behaviour and which sliders you will be living on

functions.basis: Front bias sets the restoring moment (the real stabiliser); mass sets yaw inertia (slow to start rotating AND slow to stop). They are independent, hence four quadrants rather than one axis.
functions.worked_example: Viper 3,148 lb / 54% → Self-damping GT. 4C 2,053 lb / 47% → Nervous & darty. Matches how both cars actually behaved.
functions.caveats: Wheelbase and engine placement matter as much as these two numbers and are not on the panel. The 2750 lb / 50% thresholds are this project's calibration, not game data.

functions.name: Breakaway margin — how catchable a slide is
functions.signature: breakaway_margin(friction_front_peak, friction_rear_peak at the moment of breakaway) -> margin
functions.expression: margin = rear_peak% − front_peak%, sampled on the telemetry Friction page at the frame where the rear ring turns red

output.name: margin
output.meaning: large positive = the front still has reserve while the rear is gone, so the slide is catchable; near zero = all four let go together and no one can save it

functions.basis: Recovery from oversteer requires front grip in reserve at the moment the rear exceeds its limit.
functions.status: PROPOSED — never yet measured. The Friction page's Peak % scaling is not documented; treat the comparison as ordinal (front vs rear) rather than as a calibrated number.
functions.caveats: Until it is run in-game this is a hypothesis with a procedure attached, not a result.

functions.name: PI ledger — landing exactly on a class cap
functions.expression: Find the subset of part changes whose PI deltas sum to (target_pi − current_pi), subject to every measured stat target being met simultaneously.
functions.basis: Combinatorial search over the measured parts table, constrained by the compare pane's stat targets.
functions.worked_example: Viper donor engine: needed +189 hp / +131 ft-lb over stock on the original block. No single part fit; Street Centrifugal + Race Intercooler + Race Fuel System + Race Oil/Cooling summed to 834/731 exactly, and the install confirmed it to the digit.
functions.note: Exact arithmetic over measured data — the only 'formula' here that produced a prediction later verified perfectly in-game.
functions.caveats: Part PI costs are CONFIG-DEPENDENT — the game re-prices as the build changes, so a ledger solved at one configuration must be re-previewed at the final one.

housekeeping.rule: New quantitative claims go here FIRST, with units and a tier, and prose elsewhere references them by id. If a model cannot state its units and its domain, it is not ready to be used.
housekeeping.refuted_kept_deliberately: aero_balance_ratio stays in the registry as a refuted entry so the mistake is not silently re-made.
